props.title: Almost an Angel

sections.content: Almost an Angel (1990) represents an interesting pivot point in Paul Hogan's career, coming right after his massive success with Crocodile Dundee (1986) and Crocodile Dundee II (1988). The film attempts to blend spiritual themes with Hogan's trademark Aussie charm, following a petty criminal who believes he's become a guardian angel after a near-death experience. It shares DNA with other celestial intervention films of the era like Ghost (1990) and Angels in the Outfield (1994), but with a distinctly Australian twist on the American guardian angel trope.

sections.content: The early 1990s saw a surge of spiritually-themed comedies that dealt with divine intervention, including Heart and Souls (1993) and Sister Act (1992). These films typically balanced supernatural elements with earthly humor, though Almost an Angel stands out for its more ambiguous approach to its protagonist's supposed transformation. The film's reception suffered partly because audiences expected another Crocodile Dundee-style fish-out-of-water comedy, but instead got a more contemplative piece about redemption.

Hogan's performance as Terry Dean showcases his attempt to expand beyond the larrikin persona that made him famous. The film shares thematic elements with other redemption narratives like Trading Places (1983) and Regarding Henry (1991), where near-death experiences or life-altering events transform morally questionable characters into better people. Director John Cornell, who had previously worked with Hogan on the Dundee films, attempts to maintain the star's appealing everyman quality while pushing into more philosophical territory. sections.content: The film arrived during a period when Hollywood was particularly interested in angels and divine intervention storylines. Michael (1996) would later explore similar territory with John Travolta as a chain-smoking angel, while City of Angels (1998) took a more romantic approach to celestial beings walking among humans. Almost an Angel distinguishes itself by maintaining ambiguity about whether Terry is actually an angel or simply delusional, adding an interesting layer to its exploration of faith and goodness.
